page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores with hyper-threading) operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, alongside 48 KB L1D and 2 MB L2 caches. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, making it capable of handling high-speed local read and write operations. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI flags. No GPU accelerators are present on this server.

Benchmark results show strong performance across multiple domains. Single-threaded performance is notable, with Geekbench single-core scores and gzip compression rates reaching top-tier levels. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tests, register strong performance. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 166.74 GB/sec for read operations and 65.26 GB/sec for write operations. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLM models, alongside average performance for large 70B models.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated high-speed NVMe storage, the D32ds_v7 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense general-purpose workloads. It is configured for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, text and image processing, and intermediate-scale LLM inference tasks.
